transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

This issue is most commonly caused by a blocked lint filter or vent pipe restricting airflow. You should check and clean these components first to see if drying performance improves. From what you have described, the most likely cause is clean the lint filter and the condenser/heat exchanger. Can you tell me whether filters/condenser not cleaned recently?
The door fluff filters get emptied, but I've never cleaned the condenser at the bottom. Not sure how to do it though. The clean filter symbol comes up sometimes too.

Damp laundry is most often an airflow problem, and the first free check is the fluff filter in the door opening — heat-pump models often have a second filter at the bottom too. Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), is the mesh torn, or was it already clean?
Yes the door filters had fluff and a waxy film. I rinsed them under the tap and water barely went through until I scrubbed them. Is that normal?

No, it is not normal for a tumble dryer to leave clothes damp after two hours. This indicates a fault such as a blocked condenser or venting issue that needs addressing. Overloading, or putting clothes in that weren't spun well in the washer, makes drying much slower. The drum should be no more than about two-thirds full. Was it overloaded or were the clothes very wet going in (and have you changed that), or was it a normal, well-spun load?
Normal load, 1200 spin in the washer, so not overloaded or soaking. Also uses fabric softener if that matters.

The fact that your filters had a waxy film from fabric softener is significant. That residue doesn't just stay on the door filter; it builds up inside the machine's condenser (the heat exchanger at the bottom), which blocks airflow and drastically reduces drying efficiency. This is probably why your clothes are coming out damp. Please switch off and unplug the dryer first. Locate the small access panel at the bottom right of the front face (you may need a screwdriver). Remove it to reveal the condenser unit. Reinsert it securely, replace the panel, and run a drying cycle. Let me know if you were able to access and clean this component, and whether the machine dried normally afterwards.

Got the condenser out from the bottom flap and the front was matted with lint. Rinsed it with the shower head and it came clean. Ran a test cycle after and the clothes dried in about 100 minutes, with the water container nearly full.

Check the vent hose out of the back: it should be short, without kinks or squashed sections, and clear of fluff all the way to the outside vent. Was it kinked, squashed or blocked (and is it sorted), or was it already clear?
It's a condenser model so there's no vent hose out the back as far as I know. Not sure what you mean. It's drying fine now anyway.
Good news, that has sorted it. If it happens again, start with the same check. Is there anything else I can help with?
